14.0.0.en: And I looked: a preface to the description of a new scene having no connection with what preceded.

14.0.1.en: A Lamb: a reference and symbol to the Lord Christ, to Him be glory, for He is the Lamb slain for our redemption. A hundred forty and four thousand: a reference to the multitude of the redeemed who follow Him (see ch. 7:4). His Father's name: as the followers of the beast have a mark that shows their identity and allegiance, so also the children of God have a mark, and the name of God on their foreheads, which is a free gift that we receive here by Baptism and confirm by our striving against sin, and which is completed for us in heaven.

14.0.2.en: Christ appeared on Mount Zion, which is a figure for the Church and her elevated place, because the temple of the Old Testament was built on this mountain, and also a figure for heaven and its height and the everlasting dwelling place of God (Ps 9:11). With Him also appeared His own, who received Him, believed and held fast to Him ... For God in His love for His children makes them share by His grace in His glories.

14.1.0.en: The scene of the appearance of the Lord Christ was accompanied by voices originating from heaven, and they are strong voices "

14.1.1.en: proclaiming His victory, "many waters and thunder," and gentle voices of praise proclaiming the jubilation of the heavenly creation over the Savior " "

14.1.2.en: the Redeemer, playing on harps. See also (ch. 5:8, 9).

14.2.0.en: And they sung: that is, the hundred and forty-four thousand with the heavenly creation.

14.2.1.en: A new song: that is, words that were not known, which the Holy Spirit gives to the victors, and this reminds us of what the Apostle Paul said about the language of heaven, "which it is not lawful for a man to utter" (2 Cor 12:14). Redeemed from the earth: that is, by the blood of Christ, for Christ paid His blood as the price for purchasing everyone who accepts His redemption in all the world ...

14.2.2.en: This verse shows us the special gifts that are given only to the children of God and to no others. They have the name of God (v. 1), and they now have a language of praise and a song that belongs to them and that none other knows, and they alone stand before the divine throne, always enjoying the sight and presence of God, which cannot be described and cannot be grasped by the human mind.

14.3.0.en: These two verses show the reason and causes for the distinction of these (the hundred and forty-four thousand) from the rest of the inhabitants of the world, in that they:

14.3.1.en: 1- Lived a life of purity, for the only Bridegroom of their souls is the Lord Christ and their desire is to please Him, and they did not live in the lusts of fornication like the rest of the inhabitants of the world.

14.3.2.en: 2- Follow the Lamb: their eyes and hearts are attached to Him and do not leave Him, for His place is always their place.

14.3.3.en: 3- Were redeemed from among men: they alone are those who accepted faith in Christ and lived as befits this faith, in works that please the heart of God, and became an example and firstfruits for others.

14.3.4.en: 4- In their mouth was found no guile: they imitated the Lamb, their God, "who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth" (1 Pet 2:22). All their speech is true, and they are not like the children of the evil world in their cunning and error.

14.3.5.en: 5- Without fault before the throne of God: although there is no man without sin or fault, because of their faithfulness in striving and in trying to please God, God ascribed perfection to them, so that they became without fault before Him.

14.3.6.en: My God, the Lamb slain for me .. I always desire, despite all my weaknesses, to be without fault before You, but here I am still far from You ... When shall I follow You with all my heart like these saints, and when shall I praise You with such a spiritual song? Grant me, O God, to complete the days of my sojourn in fear, for Your good pleasure, and let me enjoy You here that I may win eternity with You there on the heavenly Mount Zion.

14.4.s.en: (2) The three angels and the proclamation of judgment

14.4.0.en: A scene of a new angel flying in the midst of heaven for all the inhabitants of the earth to see, carrying " "

14.4.1.en: good news, that is, glad tidings for all who await it among the inhabitants of the earth, and at the same time it is frightening news for everyone who ignored and did not believe in the coming of the hour of judgment. His voice was strong and resounding, proclaiming the beginning of the judgment, and because of its awe and severity, prostration and contrition were required before the Owner of this hour, who is God, the Creator of heaven, earth, the sea and all that is in them.

14.4.2.en: The everlasting gospel: true news with no going back. Some also saw that it is the Holy Bible, which carries all the true promises of God.

14.5.0.en: A second angel appeared, proclaiming new news, the fall of Babylon!!...

14.5.1.en: Babylon is fallen, is fallen: Babylon symbolizes the kingdom of evil throughout the ages, and what the angel proclaimed here is the same as what the prophet Isaiah said in his prophecy, "Babylon is fallen, is fallen; and all the graven images of her gods" (Isa 21:9). The meaning is that at the proclamation of God's judgment at His Second Coming, the passing away of the kingdom of Satan, with all its soldiers and power, is also proclaimed, and it will not rise again.

14.5.2.en: She made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication: this also agrees with what the prophet Jeremiah said, "Babylon hath been a golden cup ... that made all the earth drunken: the nations have drunken of her wine ... Babylon is suddenly fallen and destroyed" (Jer 51:7, 8). The meaning is that the kingdom of evil did various evils in every direction and caused many to stumble and fall, for Satan in his wrath and rage seduced people with actual bodily fornication and drowned them in destructive lusts, or with spiritual fornication, meaning that he isolated them and separated them from God. This proclamation as a whole carries joy and victory at the end of the evil one, whose day of just judgment has come.

14.6.0.en: The first angel came proclaiming the salvation of Christ and the believers' enjoyment of Him, and the second proclaimed the just judgment of God and the passing away of the kingdom of evil and its final fall .. and now the third angel comes proclaiming the severe vengeance of God on everyone who followed Satan and became his servant.

14.6.1.en: If any man worship the beast and his image: that is, whoever worshipped Satan with direct worship, or practiced magic, or called others to leave God and worship Satan, and everyone whom Satan used to cause others to stumble. Receive his mark in his forehead, or in his hand: see (ch. 13:16). For all these the punishment of God will be very severe and terrifying.

14.6.2.en: The wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture: people were accustomed at their feasts to dilute wine with water to weaken its effect, but the word "without mixture" means "strong and concentrated without dilution," which is a figure for the severity of God's punishment of everyone who followed Satan. There is no room for God's mercies in the general judgment for whoever did not make use of them here in his life on earth.

14.6.3.en: "Shall be tormented with fire and brimstone," which burned Sodom and Gomorrah of old (Gen 19:24), and the expression confirms all that preceded of the severity of God's wrath and punishment.

14.6.4.en: In the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb: as the followers of the beast mocked and made light of heaven, God and all His believing children in His living Church, God's justice requires that His angels and His holy children enjoy the accomplishment of His justice and the defeat of the evil enemy who made them taste much torment and persecution on earth, and Christ Himself will be in the midst of His children, proclaiming His authority and victory.

14.7.0.en: The smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: a figure for the continuance of their burning without stopping and without their being consumed; for it is known that fire after a period consumes everything, and when it ends the smoke also ends shortly after it .. but here it continues without end.

14.7.1.en: They have no rest: it was customary to give the tortured a period of rest and breath before resuming their torture, but here there is no rest and no stopping. The expression day and night is figurative, since there is no night and day in eternity, but it denotes the continuance of the torment without interruption.

14.8.0.en: Here is the patience of the saints: that is, at this time God proclaims and rewards all the saints who were patient and bore all the persecution of the beast, and God shows us their reward to encourage us, making clear that the secret of their victory and patience is the strength of their faith in the Lord Jesus and their striving to act on His commandment.

14.8.1.en: My beloved brother, the frightening scene of the end of the wicked and likewise God's blessing of His holy, patient children is nothing but a message to us all that carries a warning and an encouragement: the warning of God's stern judgment on the wicked, and the encouragement for us if we stand firm in striving and holding fast to our Christ. Let us therefore hold fast to our striving, whatever the price paid here on earth, and also to our hope in the salvation of our God and His blessing of His faithful servants.

14.9.0.en: I heard a voice from heaven: this may be the voice of God or the voice of the angel who accompanied John in his vision.

14.9.1.en: God proclaims His blessing, that is, the happiness of everyone who leaves life on earth and is transferred to heaven, where their true rest and happiness begin, which is not deficient.

14.9.2.en: Their works do follow them: God indicates that His justice requires that a person be recompensed for all the works he did in his life, and this is what our Church teaches us in her belief that a person's salvation requires his faith in Christ, and likewise his good works, for which he will be recompensed in eternity with rest, happiness and blessedness.

14.10.0.en: After that St. John saw the Lord Christ wrapped in His glory, for the cloud always points to the glory of God, His purity and holiness. And because this scene is connected with the authority of the Lord Christ in the judgment of the wicked, St. John saw Him crowned with a crown of gold, as an indication of His everlasting reign. The sickle is a curved agricultural tool, like the crescent, used for reaping crops, and it is a figure for the beginning of the reaping of all mankind, and the whole scene symbolizes the beginning of the judgment. It is noted that this scene agrees completely with what the Lord Christ Himself said about the beginning of the judgment, "But when the fruit is brought forth, immediately he putteth in the sickle, because the harvest is come" (Mk 4:29).

14.11.0.en: Another angel came out of the temple: that is, he came out from before God and His presence.

14.11.1.en: Crying with a loud voice: a great and strong voice, because it suits the subject he speaks about, which is the beginning of the judgment. The word "crying" here means that he pleads earnestly and eagerly with the Lord to begin what the angels have longed to see accomplished, as have all the saints who pray every day with longing, "Thy kingdom come." The harvest of the earth is ripe: the farmer is accustomed to reaping his plants after they dry, like wheat and beans ... that is, the harvest is completely ready and its promised hour has come ...

14.11.2.en: And thrust in ... his sickle: that is, he proclaimed the beginning of His judgment and the end of life on earth.

14.12.0.en: The sickle that was in the hand of Christ represents His will and authority at the time of the beginning of the judgment, while the angel who came out with the sickle is a reference to all the angels to whom the command of execution was issued.

14.13.0.en: Another angel: other than the one carrying the sickle.

14.13.1.en: From the altar: where the prayers of the saints were with the incense (ch. 8), and where the souls of the martyrs also cried out, "How long, O Lord ... dost thou not judge and avenge our blood" (ch. 6:10). Which had power over fire: this indicates that his redemption was to gather the wicked to their place, which is the fire. The clusters of the vine of the earth: he means the wicked who completed their evils and refused repentance and so deserved the judgment of the earth.

14.13.2.en: This angel, who is responsible for the place of eternal torment, that is, the fire, proclaims to the angel carrying the sickle to begin the judgment in order to cast the wicked into the eternal fire.

14.14.0.en: And the angel thrust in his sickle: that is, the first, charged with the other angels to begin the work.

14.14.1.en: Gathered the vine of the earth: that is, the souls of mankind, which he reaped by death.

14.14.2.en: The great winepress of the wrath of God: the place prepared for the wicked, and the word winepress suggests the severity of the just divine punishment and vengeance.

14.15.0.en: The winepress was trodden: that is, the punishment began, and the literal meaning is that the process of pressing began, and the word "trodden" is the expression used for that.

14.15.1.en: Without the city: the city here is the city of God, His angels and His saints, and "without the city" is a meaning that symbolizes the impossibility of the wicked being in the presence of God during their punishment, for no wicked person approaches the holy place.

14.15.2.en: Even unto the horse bridles: the blood coming out of the winepress of the wicked became so deep that it rose from the surface of the earth to the horses' bridles, which are placed above their noses.

14.15.3.en: By the space of a thousand and six hundred furlongs: the speech here is all figurative, but the meaning intended is a confirmation of all that preceded of the severity of God's wrath and punishment of the wicked, as though their blood were not contained by a basin whose height is the noses of horses and whose area is hundreds of kilometers!!...

14.15.4.en: If the day of judgment will certainly come, let us hasten to repentance and reject every lust, however dear it is to us, and cut off all its sources, so that we escape the divine wrath and indeed enjoy His love and tenderness.

14.15.5.en: Preface to the bowls of God's wrath, introduction to the chapter: this chapter is connected with the one that follows it at one point, which is the seven bowls (plagues) of God's wrath, the last before the judgment. This chapter only refers to them, while the details come in chapter sixteen.

14.15.6.en: 1 And I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvellous, seven angels having the seven last plagues; for in them is filled up the wrath of God. 2 And I saw as it were a sea of glass mingled with fire: and them that had gotten the victory over the beast, and over his image, and over his mark, and over the number of his name, stand on the sea of glass, having the harps of God. 3 And they sing the song of Moses the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying, "Great and marvellous are thy works, Lord God Almighty; just and true are thy ways, thou King of saints. 4 Who shall not fear thee, O Lord, and glorify thy name? for thou only art holy: for all nations shall come and worship before thee; for thy judgments are made manifest."

14.15.7.en: 5 And after that I looked, and, behold, the temple of the tabernacle of the testimony in heaven was opened: 6 And the seven angels came out of the temple, having the seven plagues, clothed in pure and white linen, and having their breasts girded with golden girdles. 7 And one of the four beasts gave unto the seven angels seven golden vials full of the wrath of God, who liveth for ever and ever. 8 And the temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God, and from his power; and no man was able to enter into the temple, till the seven plagues of the seven angels were fulfilled.
